name: Recursive Language Models (RLM): DockerREPL
pinned: commit e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb (rlm 0.1.3), same clone as rlm at research/impls/rlm/repo; image python:3.11-slim
engine: CPython 3.11 in a python:3.11-slim Docker container; each cell is `docker exec python /workspace/_exec.py`, which exec()s the code with dill-persisted locals
how_run: DockerREPL(custom_tools=...) then env.execute_code(code), the call RLM makes per cell; environment='docker' in get_environment. No LLM (lm_handler_address None). Harness pins the proxy port to 41920+n and names the container rlm-docker-<probe>.

P1.detail: a host callable in custom_tools is skipped with a comment ('is a host callable and is not available in the docker environment', docker_repl.py:248-253); calling it gave NameError: name 'lookup' is not defined, 0 host calls. Passed as a code string, lookup runs inside the container and printed 42 (0 host calls).

P2.detail: execute_code returned all 200,001 chars of stdout; the last expression 'RETURNED' is dropped (exec). The RLM loop's format_iteration cuts the model view to 20,036 chars ending '... + [180002 chars...]' (rlm/utils/parsing.py, out/P2-model-view.txt)

P3.detail: printed 200 from https://example.com; the container runs on the default bridge network (docker_repl.py:530-545 passes no network flag) and setup itself pip-installs dill and requests

P4.detail: read the container's own /etc/hosts (127.0.0.1 localhost ... 0.250.250.254 host.docker.internal), not the host's. The host temp workspace is mounted read-write at /workspace.

P5.detail: printed None: docker run passes no host environment

P6.detail: docker exec is called with no timeout (docker_repl.py:705-708) and no RLM option sets one; harness stopped it at 120 s and removed the container

P7.detail: no --memory flag (docker_repl.py:530-545); harness removed the container at 4,808 MiB cgroup memory about 1.5 s into the cell. Docker Desktop VM total is 16 GB, the only ceiling.

P8.detail: execution 2 printed '7': each cell is a new python process, and _locals is dill-dumped to /workspace/state.dill between cells (docker_repl.py:323-356)

P9.detail: no host-tool bridge for custom tools. lookup as a code string inside the container: loop 1,022 ms, 5 threads 207 ms, 0 host calls. Only llm_query/rlm_query cross to the host, over the HTTP proxy.

P10.detail: stderr: 'Traceback ... File "/workspace/_exec.py", line 109 ... File "<string>", line 1, in <module>\nValueError: probe-boom'; message and line survive

P11.detail: same env, one docker exec per cell: median 215 ms, p90 389 ms (n=20); setup (docker run + pip install dill requests) 3254 ms; fresh env incl. setup [3356, 3567, 2784, 3582, 2719] ms

P12.detail: subclass walk ran (443 classes, 1 _wrap_close); __import__('os').system and _wrap_close.__init__.__globals__['system'] both returned 0, inside the container. No docker.sock, no /Users. Two host-facing paths exist: the sandbox wrote a file into the host-mounted workspace (seen on the host), and it reached the host proxy at host.docker.internal (answered 'No LM handler configured').

defaults.time: None. execute_code runs docker exec with no timeout (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:705-708); RLM max_timeout is checked only between iterations (rlm.py:421-422). P6 ran to the 120 s harness stop.
defaults.memory: None. docker run has no --memory/--cpus/--pids-limit (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:530-545). P7 reached 4,808 MiB before the harness kill.
defaults.output: execute_code returns all stdout uncapped (200,001 chars); the RLM loop caps the model view at 20,000 chars per block, head only, with a "... + [N chars...]" marker (rlm/utils/parsing.py).
defaults.tool_calls: No custom-tool bridge (host callables skipped). llm_query/rlm_query go through a host ThreadingHTTPServer proxy; rlm_query_batched is capped at max_concurrent_subcalls=4.
defaults.hardened_null_reason: DockerREPL exposes only `image` (plus shared env args); it has no timeout, memory, CPU, network or mount option (docker_repl.py:431-452, 530-545; docs/src/app/environments/docker/page.tsx:43-50), so there is no stricter configuration to run.

source_notes.finding: No stricter option exists. DockerREPL takes only `image` plus the shared env arguments (docker_repl.py:431-452); docs list image, setup_code, context_payload, lm_handler_address (docs/src/app/environments/docker/page.tsx:43-50). There is no timeout, memory, CPU, network or read-only flag to set, so hardened is null.

custom_tools values that are code strings are pasted into the per-cell script; plain data is JSON-loaded; host callables are dropped with a warning comment. The model sees tool names and descriptions via format_tools_for_prompt.
All custom tools are listed upfront in the system prompt; no search.

Only llm_query/llm_query_batched/rlm_query/rlm_query_batched cross the boundary: container code POSTs to http://host.docker.internal:<port>, a ThreadingHTTPServer on the host bound to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), which forwards to the LM handler socket. LM credentials stay on the host.

A Docker container, default bridge network, running as root (python:3.11-slim default user), with the host temp workspace bind-mounted read-write at /workspace. The module docstring says "fully isolated from the host LM process"; the README groups docker with non-isolated local environments. P4/P5/P12 stayed in the container; the sandbox can write the host workspace and call the proxy.
stdout and stderr captured in the container script and returned in a JSON line; last expression dropped; RLM caps the model view at 20,000 chars.
None in DockerREPL: no exec timeout, no container limits, no output cap at the env level.
Persists across cells through /workspace/state.dill; values that dill cannot pickle are silently dropped.
traceback.print_exc into stderr, so the model sees the full traceback with line numbers (line 109 is the harness exec line, line 1 the user code).
E2B, Modal, Daytona and Prime backends (e2b_repl.py, modal_repl.py, daytona_repl.py, prime_repl.py) need accounts and API keys: blocked-needs-credentials, not probed.

surprises: Host callables passed as custom_tools are silently replaced by a comment in the container script; the first call fails with NameError. Tools must be source strings, so any credentials a tool needs must be inside the container.
The LM proxy binds 0.0.0.0 on an OS-chosen port (docker_repl.py:512-520), so other machines on the network can reach llm_query while a session runs.
Each setup runs pip install dill requests inside the container, so the default needs network, and setup took about 3.3 s.
No execution timeout anywhere: an infinite loop holds the RLM iteration forever.
